newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks end up as strong economic growth seen.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks end up as strong economic growth seen.

text.p: The Lima stock exchange closed higher Wednesday as players estimated forthcoming government figures would show the country on course for strong economic growth this year, brokers said.
The hope that this growth would translate into solid company profits was set to lift the market again Thursday, they added.

Wednesday, the General Index rose 0.73 percent to 2,076.8 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index edged up 1.69 percent to 3,036.4 points, according to preliminary figures given at the market's close.
The Selective Index closed for the first time above the 3,000 point mark. In a total of 2,360 trades, volume was 42.8 million soles ($16.2 million), brokers said.

"All the expectations are sending money into public sector firms, especially in the electricity and telecommunications areas," said Jorge Gutierrez of local brokerage Corin, adding the mining sector's record bull run appeared to be dying out.
The government is set to publish early next week statistics for April's gross domestic product (GDP) growth, which the market expected to record the highest figure of the year, brokers said.
Electricity distributor, Moyopampa -- formerly known as Edegel -- rose 4.14 percent to 1.51 soles, on strong volume of 3.19 million shares.
Peru's largest brewery group Unin de Cerveceras Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA rose 2.50 percent to 2.46 soles on volume of 1.65 million shares.
Investors continued to take profits in Atacocha after its record bull run this month. The polymetallic miner fell 2.46 percent to 2.38 soles on volume of 872,000 shares
